intro: thanks for looking after the menagerie!

house_notes.title: Important locations
items: All dog and cat food lives in the kitchen side closet — senior dry, high-protein dry, large-dog dry, wet food cans, plus the measuring cups (sitting on top of the wet food).
Ziggy's and Boomba's meds live on the kitchen counter.
Communal water jug in the kitchen — every dog and cat drinks from it. Keep it topped up.
Cat free-feed bowls are in the window bay in the living room — Finn, Ellie + Cabbage all eat there.

Litter boxes (the Litter Robots) are in the downstairs bathroom — they're self-cleaning, nothing to do. That bathroom also has the blockade that keeps Ziggy out, so use the upstairs bathroom yourself.
Chicken feed bin (black, near the coop gate) — bag of laying pellets and the scattering bowl live inside. The bowl is just a scoop — you toss the feed over the fence so it lands on the hay.

Chickens are in three spots: the coop (Colin + the hens), the front-yard chicken tractor next to the coop (a mother hen with 3 chicks, plus a few teenagers who kept escaping the coop — locked in for the weekend), and the dog-yard chicken tractor (the roosters).

house_notes.title: Feeding quirks
items: Wet dog food split: half to Ziggy, half to Lucy, with a quarter of Lucy's half going to Bear.
Finn, Ellie + Cabbage free-feed all day; just keep the window-bay bowls topped up from the closet.
The roosters are pre-stocked — no feeding needed during the trip. Just glance to confirm food + water look fine.
Pellets: the coop gets one and a half bowls, the front-yard tractor (mum, chicks + teenagers) gets one large bowl — both from the same black bin, same time. Tractor water is fine for the trip.
Eggs from the hens — take as many as you'd like, or leave them. No pressure either way.

house_notes.title: Watch-outs
items: Ziggy: 7 pills in the morning wrapped in a cheese slice (1 mycophenolate, 2 gabapentin, 4 clonidine), then 1 mycophenolate + fish oil in his evening wet food. The purple mycophenolate is the one that really matters.
Boomba: 2 methimazole in his morning wet food, 1 in the evening. Watch him eat them — Finn tries to steal his wet food.
Raccoons have been around — double-check the chicken shed is closed by sundown (Colin usually puts everyone to bed, but verify).
Bear shouldn't be outside alone — raccoons and coyotes leave Lucy + Ziggy together alone, but Bear solo is fair game. Supervise him.

Bear & Lucy get a little cheese too if they're nearby.

Dogs usually want a second outdoor session.

Pre-dinner outside session for Ziggy & Lucy

event.text: Evening feed for Boomba — 1 pill hidden in his wet food.

pets.name: Boomba

feeding.when: Twice daily — morning (with Ziggy's cheese pill, ~9:00 AM) and evening (with the dogs' dinner, ~10:30 PM)
feeding.where: Downstairs hallway — his bowl sits on the tiled surface near the basement stairs, directly opposite the kitchen side closet.
feeding.what: Wet food — half a container in the morning, the other half in the evening, with his methimazole hidden in each half (see Medication).
feeding.notes: He will demand food and try to trick you into feeding him more. Don't fall for it. Watch that the pills actually go down, and keep Finn off his bowl — Finn will happily lick the wet-food butter knife instead.

meds.schedule: Methimazole (hot pink) — 2 pills in the morning, 1 in the evening, hidden in his wet food
meds.morning: Hide 2 hot pink methimazole in his morning half-container of wet food — same time as Ziggy's cheese ball.
meds.evening: Hide 1 hot pink methimazole in his evening half-container of wet food — same time as the dogs' dinner.
meds.notes: Watch him eat — he sometimes leaves the pills, and Finn will try to steal his wet food. Letting Finn lick the wet-food butter knife keeps him busy and away from Boomba.

quirks: If you sit, he will sit on you.
Loud purring while sitting on you = he's about to bite. You have been warned.
Ignore him a bit and he gets snuggly. Pat him too much and he bites.
Mostly bites people who like cats.
warnings: may try to dart outside — he's fast
if he escapes, he hides under the deck (he doesn't go far)

pets.name: Cabbage

feeding.where: Living room window bay — same free-feed bowls as Finn and Ellie.
feeding.what: Dry cat food, kept topped up from the kitchen side closet.

quirks: Likes her blue chair and her CD shelf. Otherwise prefers to be left alone.
Sometimes confuses Bear for a cat and tries to clean him. Very cute.
Does not like being picked up by strangers.
warnings: can be bullied by Ellie — keep an eye on their interactions

pets.name: Ziggy
pets.tagline: world's largest lap dog. sensitive soul.

feeding.where: Kitchen — his bowl sits on a wooden stand right next to the communal water jug.
feeding.what: Fill his bowl (on the wooden stand) with large-dog dry food. Evening: add half a can of wet food on top, with his mycophenolate + fish oil capsule pushed into the wet food.
feeding.notes: Half the wet can is Ziggy's; the other half splits between Lucy and Bear.

meds.schedule: Morning: 1 mycophenolate + 2 gabapentin + 4 clonidine (in cheese). Evening: 1 mycophenolate + 1 fish oil (in wet food).
meds.location: Kitchen counter. Cheese slices are in the fridge, bottom drawer.
meds.morning: Wrap 1 purple mycophenolate, 2 brown/cream gabapentin and 4 light pink clonidine in a cheese slice, roll it into a ball and put it in his bowl. Bear and Lucy get a little cheese too if they're around.
meds.evening: Push 1 purple mycophenolate + 1 fish oil capsule into his wet food.
meds.notes: Make sure he eats every pill — the purple mycophenolate is the one that really matters. If he spits one out, wrap it in more cheese and try again.

quirks: Sometimes scared to go outside — be patient.
Scared of storms. Scratching his butt calms him down.

pets.name: Bear
pets.tagline: old man. couch enthusiast. very small.

feeding.where: Under the plants near the front door — the little cubby below the plant window is his eating spot.
feeding.what: Fill his small metal bowl about 1/4 full with senior dry food (kitchen side closet) + a small dollop of wet food — about a quarter of Lucy's half of the can.
feeding.notes: Needs to go outside for the toilet right after eating — and Bear outside means human supervision. Bear sleeps in the small towel-covered crate in the living room, near his eating cubby. He needs ~4 of the treats in the bag on the plant shelf to be coaxed in there. Keep the door shut for his sleeping hours so the cats dont bully him out.

quirks: Loves sitting outside with Lucy to relax.
Sleeps in a small towel-covered crate in the living room, near his eating cubby — door shut overnight because he pees on things if he wanders the house. Treats on top of the crate help lure him in.
If you're heading out for more than an hour during the day, crate him too — same wandering-and-peeing problem.

pets.name: Lucy

feeding.where: Kitchen, near the fridge. When she's done, put her bowl back next to Ziggy's wooden stand.
feeding.what: Fill her bowl about 1/2 full with high-protein dry food + half a can of wet food on top.
feeding.notes: Wet can splits: Ziggy gets half, Lucy gets half, Bear gets a quarter of Lucy's half.

quirks: Might bark a little when you first arrive — she's a lover underneath.
A bit afraid of strange men, but warms up quickly.
Loves chilling outside with Bear.

pets.name: Ellie

feeding.where: Living room window bay — Finn, Ellie and Cabbage share the free-feed bowls in there.
feeding.what: Dry cat food, kept topped up from the kitchen side closet.

quirks: Spends most of her time upstairs unless she's in the mood to bully Cabbage.
Ragdoll-ish but prefers riding on your shoulder over being carried.
Confident and playful.
warnings: may bully Cabbage — give Cabbage space if Ellie is around

pets.name: Finn

feeding.where: Living room window bay — Finn, Ellie and Cabbage share the free-feed bowls in there.
feeding.what: Dry cat food, kept topped up from the kitchen side closet.

quirks: Will run into any open door.
Sometimes gets himself trapped inside cupboards or stuck outside.
Pure love muffin energy.
warnings: watch open doors — he goes through them all

pets.name: The Hens
pets.tagline: the coop flock, Colin the rooster included.

feeding.when: Once between 8:00 AM and noon. If you had to lure an escapee back in with food, just scatter a little extra over the fence afterward.
feeding.where: The black bin near the coop gate holds the pellets and the scattering bowl. Scoop the feed with the bowl and toss it over the fence onto the hay — the hens eat off the ground, not from a bowl.
feeding.what: Coop: one and a half bowls of laying pellets — toss over the fence so it scatters across the hay. Front-yard tractor: one large bowl of pellets for mum, the chicks and the teenagers.
feeding.notes: Water is automated — just glance to confirm it's flowing. The tractor birds' water is fine for the trip too.

quirks: Colin the rooster and the hens live in the coop. The front-yard chicken tractor next to it holds a mother hen with 3 chicks plus a few teenagers who kept escaping the coop — they're locked in for the weekend. Mum bullies the teenagers a little; they can deal with it.
Fat Face (the black one) and Karen (the pure white one) might escape — toss extra food in, open the door, and chase them back in.
Colin does a great job putting everyone to bed.
warnings: raccoons have been around — confirm the whole flock is in the shed by sundown
automated door usually closes itself, but verify

pets.name: The Roosters

feeding.when: No feeding needed during the trip.
feeding.where: The chicken tractor in the dog yard.
feeding.what: Pre-stocked with food and water. Just glance to confirm levels look OK; top up only if something looks empty.

quirks: Priscilla is the small fancy one. Alta Vista is the large black one.
Mostly chill, will go crazy if they see a hen.
Priscilla might try to bite. But Priscilla is very small.
warnings: if you go inside their house, Priscilla (the small one) will try to escape — block the door

timeline_note: These are just estimates — we're pretty loose with times. Nothing here is strict.
